note: One entry per concept video. The video session fills "studio" (the Canvas Studio embed link) and sets "status" to "recorded" and "minutes" to the true length when a video is done; build_concepts_page.py turns this file into index.html. No course numbers, test names or dates in any field: the videos stand alone.

stages.name: Question
stages.line: What do you want to know, for whom, and is it a prediction or an effect?

stages.name: Data
stages.line: Where the rows came from, who is in them, and who is missing.

stages.name: Clean
stages.line: Types, dates, missing values, joins, and the test set kept out of sight.

stages.name: Explore
stages.line: Look before you model, and know what a picture can and cannot tell you.

stages.name: Model
stages.line: The estimator or the learner, and the assumption each one rests on.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.line: How wrong could you be, and on data the model never saw?

stages.name: Communicate
stages.line: One number with its interval, one chart that does not mislead.

concepts.title: Regression for prediction and regression for inference
concepts.answers: The same fitted line does two different jobs, and the job decides what you check.

concepts.title: Random assignment as an estimator
concepts.answers: Why a coin flip turns a difference in means into an estimate of a causal effect.

concepts.title: Statistical power
concepts.answers: How many observations you need before you look, and what an underpowered study can and cannot find.

concepts.title: Sampling bias
concepts.answers: Why a huge sample can still give the wrong answer when the people in it chose to be there.

concepts.title: Train-test split and leakage
concepts.answers: Why a model must be scored on data it never saw, and the quiet ways test information leaks into training.

concepts.title: Confounding and causal diagrams
concepts.answers: How to draw the story behind the data and read off which variables to control for, and which not to.

concepts.title: Difference-in-differences
concepts.answers: How two groups and two periods estimate an effect when nothing was randomized, and the parallel-trends bet it rests on.

concepts.title: Instrumental variables
concepts.answers: How a variable that moves the treatment and nothing else recovers a causal effect, and why a weak one is worse than none.

concepts.title: Regression discontinuity
concepts.answers: Why a cutoff rule is a natural experiment for the people just either side of it.

concepts.title: Regularization: ridge and lasso
concepts.answers: How shrinking coefficients buys a little bias for a lot less variance, and why you standardize first.

concepts.title: Logistic regression
concepts.answers: How to model a yes-or-no outcome as a probability and read a coefficient on the odds scale.

concepts.title: The p-value
concepts.answers: What a p-value measures, what it does not, and why 0.049 and 0.051 are the same news.

concepts.title: The permutation test
concepts.answers: How shuffling the labels gives you a p-value with no distribution assumed.

concepts.title: The bias-variance trade-off
concepts.answers: Why a model that fits the data you have can predict the data you do not have worse, and where the sweet spot sits.

concepts.title: Precision, recall and the ROC curve
concepts.answers: Why accuracy misleads when one class is rare, and how to choose a cutoff for the mistake you care about.

concepts.title: Bootstrap confidence intervals
concepts.answers: How to put an interval around an estimate when there is no formula for its standard error.
